prompt: A service's memory climbs steadily for days until it's killed for running out of memory, then the cycle starts again after restart.
why: Monotonic growth reset only by restart is the signature of a leak. Take heap snapshots at two points and compare.
trap: It ends in exhaustion, but raising the limit just delays the crash.

prompt: Open database connections from one app grow by a few every hour and never drop, even overnight when traffic is near zero.
tells: grow by a few every hour and never drop
even overnight when traffic is near zero
why: Connections are opened on some code path and never returned; look for error paths that skip close().
trap: Usage that doesn't fall when load falls isn't load; it's a leak.

prompt: A Go service's goroutine count rises from 200 to 90,000 over a week, and each request that times out seems to add a few.
tells: rises from 200 to 90,000 over a week
why: Goroutines blocked forever on a channel or call with no cancellation. Propagate context timeouts.
trap: Many goroutines can look like contention, but the count never coming down marks a leak.

prompt: A worker's /tmp grows by about 2 GB a day and is only cleared when the container is replaced.
tells: grows by about 2 GB a day
only cleared when the container is replaced
why: Temp files are written and never deleted; clean them up in a finally block.
trap: The disk will fill eventually, but the cause is the steady leak.

prompt: A single-page app gets slower the longer a tab stays open, and memory snapshots show thousands of copies of the same event handler.
tells: the longer a tab stays open
thousands of copies of the same event handler
why: Handlers are added on every view change and never removed.
trap: Slowness that grows with time open is a leak signature.

prompt: Open file descriptors grow only on requests that hit an error path. Successful requests close everything.
tells: grow only on requests that hit an error path
why: A missing close in the error branch; use try/finally or a with-block.
trap: The eventual "too many open files" is exhaustion; the cause is a leak.

prompt: An in-process cache keyed by user ID has no size limit or expiry, and memory grows with every new user ever seen.
tells: grows with every new user ever seen
why: A cache without eviction is a leak with good intentions.
trap: It's not stale data; it's data never let go.

prompt: A service is restarted every night "for stability". When the restart was skipped for a holiday, it crashed on day three.
why: Nightly restarts were masking a slow leak.
trap: A restart schedule is a workaround, not a fix.
